messages.author: 0e34c2c2095cac59
messages.subject: trouble with grouped box plots
parts:
There is an Sweave version of the following at
http://mickmcquaid.com/non-distracting-boxplots.pdf
http://mickmcquaid.com/non-distracting-boxplots.Rnw

My objective is to obtain box and whiskers plots with
minimal ink using ggplot2.
I can do a simple example but, once I try to add some
grouping, I can not get it right.

I begin by loading the package and the data set
used in the book.
rm(list=ls())
library(ggplot2)

A sample of the data I'm using can be obtained by saying
b<-read.table("http://mickmcquaid.com/sample",header=T)

I can produce the desired box and whiskers plot as
follows, but it contains distracting extra ink. In
particular, I regard the frames around the boxes to be
extra and it would be nice if I could eliminate black
ink altogether.
bpl<-ggplot(b,aes(factor(j),i))
print(bpl+geom_boxplot(aes(fill=k)))

For example, make the median a blank line and let the
quartiles be defined by the edges of the box body, and
the lines to the extremes be the same color as the body
of each box. It would also be nice for outliers to
match the box color (the actual data set is much larger
than this sample and there are outliers of each
color---I'd like to distinguish between them quickly and
easily).

I can give a rough idea of what I want by using the
mtcars data in the ggplot2 package.
This has one slight problem with the legend that I can
see but don't understand. It's also using the huge line
width to disguise points between the quartiles and the
extremes. So it's kind of a kludge.
p<-ggplot(mtcars,aes(factor(cyl),mpg))
print(p+geom_boxplot(aes(fill=cyl,colour=cyl,size=1.9))+geom_point(aes
(colour=mtcars$cyl))+stat_summary
(fun.y=median,geom="crossbar",ymin=0,ymax=0,color="grey90"))

I tried to apply this same idea to my dataset, but can't
seem to get the groups right (I just get the median by
factor), nor can I see how to color the outliers
(they're still black). Here's one attempt with these
problems.
bpl <- ggplot(b, aes(factor(j), i))
print(bpl +
geom_boxplot(aes(fill=k,colour=k,size=1.9)) +
stat_summary
(fun.y=median,geom="crossbar",ymin=-1.0,ymax=1.0,color="grey90"))

I appreciate any help you can offer!

- Mick

parts:
> For example, make the median a blank line and let the
> quartiles be defined by the edges of the box body, and
> the lines to the extremes be the same color as the body
> of each box.  It would also be nice for outliers to
> match the box color (the actual data set is much larger
> than this sample and there are outliers of each
> color---I'd like to distinguish between them quickly and
> easily).
>
> I can give a rough idea of what I want by using the
> mtcars data in the ggplot2 package.
> This has one slight problem with the legend that I can
> see but don't understand.  It's also using the huge line
> width to disguise points between the quartiles and the
> extremes.  So it's kind of a kludge.
> p<-ggplot(mtcars,aes(factor(cyl),mpg))
> print(p+geom_boxplot(aes(fill=cyl,colour=cyl,size=1.9))+geom_point(aes
> (colour=mtcars$cyl))+stat_summary
> (fun.y=median,geom="crossbar",ymin=0,ymax=0,color="grey90"))

A couple of small fixes:

ggplot(mtcars, aes(factor(cyl), mpg)) +
geom_boxplot(aes(fill = cyl, colour = cyl), size = 1.9) +
geom_point(aes(colour = cyl))+
stat_summary(fun.y = median, geom = "crossbar", ymin = 0, ymax = 0,
color = "grey90")

* when you set the size (rather than mapping it to a variable), it
should be outside of aes
* you shouldn't use the dataset name in the aesthetic specification
* it'seasiertoreadwithspaces ;)

> I tried to apply this same idea to my dataset, but can't
> seem to get the groups right (I just get the median by
> factor), nor can I see how to color the outliers
> (they're still black).  Here's one attempt with these
> problems.
> bpl <- ggplot(b, aes(factor(j), i))
> print(bpl +
>      geom_boxplot(aes(fill=k,colour=k,size=1.9)) +
>      stat_summary
> (fun.y=median,geom="crossbar",ymin=-1.0,ymax=1.0,color="grey90"))

If you're going to take this approach, it's much easier to work with
facetting, rather than dodging:

ggplot(b, aes(k, i)) +
geom_boxplot(aes(fill = k, colour = k), size = 1.9) +
stat_summary(fun.y = median, fun.ymax = median, fun.ymin = median,
geom = "crossbar", color = "grey90") + facet_grid(. ~ j)

(also note how I set the minimum and maximum values of the crossbar to
the median - a bit of a hack but it works)

Getting the outliers on the plot is a bit more tricky. The best way
is just to calculate them yourself:

out <- ddply(b, c("j", "k"), function(df) {
data.frame(i = boxplot.stats(df$i)$out)
})

ggplot(b, aes(k, i, fill = k, colour = k)) +
geom_boxplot(size = 1.9, outlier.colour = NA) +
stat_summary(fun.y = median, fun.ymax = median, fun.ymin = median,
geom = "crossbar", color = "grey90") +
geom_point(data = out) +
facet_grid(. ~ j)

Hadley


--
http://had.co.nz/

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: trouble with grouped box plots
parts:
Maybe it's just easier to do it all by hand, and drop geom_boxplot altogether:

b <- read.table("http://mickmcquaid.com/unevensample",header=T)
out <- ddply(b, c("j", "k"), summarise, out = boxplot.stats(i,coef=1.4)$out)

stats <- ddply(b, c("j", "k"), function(df) boxplot.stats(df$i,coef=1.4)$stats)
names(stats)[-(1:2)] <- c("lwhisker", "lhinge", "med", "uhinge", "uwhisker")

ggplot(stats, aes(k, med, fill = k, colour = k)) +
geom_segment(aes(xend = k, y = lwhisker, yend = uwhisker)) +
geom_crossbar(aes(ymin = lhinge, ymax = uhinge)) +
geom_crossbar(aes(ymin = med, ymax = med), color = "grey90") +
geom_point(aes(y = out), out) +
facet_grid(. ~ j)

What do you think?

Hadley
